_what: The fixture identities the data package names, with their UUIDs fixed. §12.6: the real UUIDs are defined in the fixture catalog and a test must never generate them.
_why_derived: Each UUID is uuid5(DNS, 'thinkbizthai.fixture.<symbol>') — a pure function of the symbol. Anyone can recompute them; nobody has to trust this file to be the original. A random UUID pasted here would be an unverifiable constant, and a test that generates its own is a test whose failures cannot be reproduced. The cross-tenant assertion in particular needs workspace_b's id to be KNOWN to the attacker's side of the test: proving A cannot reach B by guessing is worthless, proving A cannot reach B while holding B's exact id is the actual control.

ai_model_openai_text.role: the GLOBAL curated model registry row, provider `openai`. It carries no _a or _b suffix for the reason industry_pack_interior carries none: every other symbol here ends in the workspace its row lives in, and a suffix would assert a tenant boundary the row does not have. Its `model_key` is the SYNTHETIC `fixture-text-model` and not a real model id, because OPEN-004 -- BYOK model allowlist and max budget -- is OPEN and §15 forbids an agent choosing an open decision; a fixture naming a real model would read as one having been chosen. Batch 060 addresses it from both tenants, from the service identity and from anonymous, and the assertion is never 'A cannot reach B's row' -- it is that no request-path identity reaches the catalog at all and the one role holding a grant is refused by row level security. It is also the row BOTH workspaces' model policies pin, which is the only way this batch can assert the catalog is global rather than replicated per tenant, since no client identity may read it directly.

billing_plan_starter.role: the GLOBAL billing plan catalog row, plan_code `starter_th_monthly_v1` -- the code §5.3 of the Stripe billing contract uses in its own example plan document. It carries no _a or _b suffix for the reason industry_pack_interior carries none: every other symbol here ends in the workspace its row lives in, and a suffix on this one would assert a tenant boundary the row does not have. Batch 130's cases attack it from BOTH tenants, from anonymous and from the service identity, and the assertion is never 'A cannot reach B's row' -- it is 'no request-path identity reaches the plan catalog at all, and the one role holding a grant is refused by row level security'.

billing_plan_starter_v1.role: revision 1 of billing_plan_starter: the published plan contract, carrying the PRICE. GLOBAL and immutable, and the row workspace_a and workspace_b are BOTH subscribed to -- which is what proves the plan catalog is global rather than replicated per tenant, since each owner sees only their own subscription while both name this one id. It is also the row every immutability case addresses, because a price is the one value in this schema whose history being rewritable would change what somebody was charged.

billing_invoice_a.role: the invoice of workspace_a, settled, with a succeeded charge and a partial refund against it. It carries a symbol where a webhook receipt and a payment do not, and the rule is this catalog's own: a receipt is addressed by (provider, livemode, event digest) and a payment by (provider, livemode, payment digest), both unique constraints in 131_billing_projection.sql spelled out of text the fixture and the case file share -- while an INVOICE's id is a value ANOTHER ROW MUST NAME, because app.billing_payments reaches it through a composite foreign key over (workspace_id, id) and a second one over (id, livemode). That is exactly the case batch 050 recorded for an outbox event, and it is the only kind of row this catalog admits a symbol for once a natural key exists.

billing_invoice_b.role: the invoice of workspace_b, held by its EXACT id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them -- and not by user_owner_b either, which is what makes batch 131's refusal a claim about the table rather than about a tenant boundary. It is deliberately UNSETTLED where billing_invoice_a is settled, and its only payment row FAILED: the two invoices differ in the column an owner would most want to read, so the pair is two distinguishable rows rather than two copies, and the failed row is what makes `failure_code`'s CHECK -- a code belongs to a failure -- satisfied in both directions by real rows.

business_a1.role: business under workspace_a, inside the editor and approver scope

business_a2.role: second business under workspace_a, deliberately OUTSIDE the editor scope

business_a3_archived.role: third business under workspace_a, archived. §11.3 says archive closes new creation under a Business while its history stays readable, and batch 020's page INSERT policy refuses a Page under it. Added by batch 020 rather than reusing business_a2, whose whole purpose is to be the Business the editor's scope excludes (batch 021); one fixture row carrying two unrelated controls is how a test starts failing for the other one's reason.

business_a4_unassigned.role: fourth business under workspace_a, live and DELIBERATELY UNASSIGNED. Added by batch 030 because that batch's permitted INSERT needs a live Business with no industry assignment, while every other live Business in workspace_a must HAVE one: business_a1 so the scoped-editor and cross-tenant positives address a row that exists, business_a2 so `editor-a-scope-does-not-reach-the-industry-assignment-of-business-a2` is a negative about a policy rather than about a missing row. business_a3_archived cannot serve either purpose, because the INSERT policy refuses a new row under an archived Business (§11.3) and that refusal is its own case. One fixture row carrying two unrelated controls is how a case starts failing for the other one's reason.

business_b1.role: business under workspace_b, reachable only by user_owner_b

user_admin_a.role: active ADMIN of workspace_a, scoped to business_a1. Added by batch 061, and it is the first identity this catalog carries for §7's second built-in role: §12.6 names an owner, an editor, an approver, a viewer and a suspended member, and no admin. §8.4 marks "Usage/quota summary SELECT" `Y` for the OWNER AND FOR THE ADMIN -- two unconditional cells, not one and a `P` -- so app.quota_buckets' SELECT policy resolves `app.workspace_member_role(workspace_id) in ('owner','admin')` and the admin half of that predicate could be asserted by no identity §12.6 names. It is SCOPED to business_a1 on purpose and the owner deliberately is not: batch 021 reads §7 as "a member with no scope row is not narrowed", so proving that batch 061's RESTRICTIVE narrowing subtracts anything at all needs a caller who passes the permissive policy AND holds a scope row, and the owner is the control for the other half.

quota_bucket_a_all.role: the WORKSPACE-LEVEL quota bucket of workspace_a: business_profile_id is NULL. It exists because batch 061's restrictive policy has an explicit NULL branch -- 021's "a WORKSPACE row is not inside any of [the scope types]" -- and a branch no row exercises is a branch that could be inverted without any case failing. user_admin_a, who IS narrowed, must still read it.

quota_bucket_a1.role: the quota bucket of workspace_a scoped to business_a1, which is INSIDE user_admin_a's member scope. The positive half of the narrowing: without it, `admin-a-cannot-read-the-quota-bucket-outside-their-narrowing` would be satisfied by a policy that denied the admin everything.

quota_bucket_a2.role: the quota bucket of workspace_a scoped to business_a2, which is OUTSIDE user_admin_a's member scope -- business_a2 exists precisely to be the Business a scope excludes (batch 021). §8.6 case 3 at Business granularity, on a table whose caller has already passed the role predicate, so the refusal can only be the restrictive policy.

quota_bucket_b.role: the workspace-level quota bucket of workspace_b. It is the row workspace_a's owner holds the exact id of and cannot read (§8.6 case 5), and the row user_owner_b CAN read -- the pair is what stops the cross-tenant negative being satisfied by a policy that denies everyone.

usage_event_a1.role: the `usage_id` of a ledger row in workspace_a. CTR-USG-001 makes usage_id the envelope's identity and app.usage_events has no other natural key a case could spell out of ids this catalog already fixes -- its dedupe_key is composed from a job_id, which would be one more constant rather than one fewer. NO REQUEST-PATH IDENTITY MAY READ IT: the row exists so that `service-sees-zero-usage-events` is about a row rather than about an empty table, which is what the CI negative control for app.usage_events rests on.

usage_event_b1.role: the same, in workspace_b. Two tenants, because no client role holds a privilege on app.usage_events at all, so this suite's substitute for a cross-tenant claim is batch 030's and 140's -- both owners are refused identically, at the privilege layer -- and that substitute is about two real rows or it is about nothing.

usage_reservation_a1.role: a hold in workspace_a, addressed by its own id because a reservation has no natural key any document fixes (batch 061's header records why inventing one would contradict CTR-USG-001). There is deliberately NO B-side reservation: §8 has no row for a reservation in any of its four matrices, so there is no cell for a both-owners-refused-identically substitute to be about, and this row exists only so that `service-sees-zero-usage-reservations` -- the case the CI negative control rests on -- addresses a row rather than an empty table.

industry_pack_interior.role: the GLOBAL industry pack catalog row, `th.sme.interior-built-in`. It carries no _a or _b suffix and that is the point: every other symbol here ends in the workspace it lives in, because every other row is tenant-owned, and a suffix on this one would assert a tenant boundary the row does not have. Batch 030's cases attack it from BOTH tenants and from the service identity, and the assertion is never 'A cannot reach B's row' -- it is 'no request-path identity reaches it at all, and the one role holding a grant is refused by row level security'.

industry_pack_interior_v1.role: published version 1.0.0 of industry_pack_interior. GLOBAL and immutable, and the row business_a1 and business_b1 are BOTH pinned to -- which is what proves the catalog is global rather than replicated per tenant, since each owner sees only their own assignment while both name this one id.

industry_pack_interior_v2.role: published version 1.1.0 of industry_pack_interior, the minor release §4.5 activates by explicit approval. GLOBAL and immutable. It exists so a re-pin has a target that is not the row already pinned: an UPDATE case that set the value the row already held would pass against a database where the write did nothing.

knowledge_a1_business.role: BUSINESS-LEVEL knowledge under business_a1: page_context_profile_id is NULL. Added by batch 040, the first family whose scope is TWO columns -- §4 invariant 3 makes Business scope mandatory and Page scope a nullable OVERRIDE -- so the fixture has to carry both states or the override is untested. This is the un-overridden one: the row every A-side positive reads and the row the approver's refused UPDATE is witnessed against. Its kind is `voice`.

knowledge_a1_page.role: PAGE-LEVEL knowledge under business_a1, restricted to page_a1. The overridden state, and the row user_page_editor_a reaches. Its kind is `audience`, because the four values §5 names are loaded across these five rows so the vocabulary is live rather than merely permitted by a CHECK.

knowledge_a1_sibling_page.role: PAGE-LEVEL knowledge under business_a1, restricted to page_a1_sibling. §8.6 case 4 at knowledge granularity -- same Business, allowed Page A, row Page B -- which no earlier fixture row can carry, because a knowledge item is the first row in this schema whose Page scope is a property of the row itself rather than of its parent. user_page_editor_a is refused it and user_editor_a, whose scope is the whole Business, is not. Its kind is `offers`.

knowledge_a2_business.role: BUSINESS-LEVEL knowledge under business_a2, deliberately outside user_editor_a's member scope. §8.6 case 3 at knowledge granularity, paired with an unscoped-owner positive so the negative is about the restrictive policy rather than about a row nobody can see. Its kind is `restrictions`, the fourth and last of §5's values.

audit_log_a1.role: the tenant audit record of workspace_a. Its ACTOR IS user_editor_a, which is the whole reason it needs a symbol rather than being addressed by its workspace: §8.4 marks "Tenant audit SELECT" `O` for the editor -- own rows -- so `editor-a-cannot-read-their-own-audit-log` is the one case in the suite where the reader IS the subject of the record, and it would be indistinguishable from the viewer's `N` if the actor were anybody else. Its outcome is `succeeded` and it carries no error_code, which is one side of CTR-AUD-001's allOf[1]/allOf[2] biconditional.

audit_log_b1.role: the tenant audit record of workspace_b, held by its EXACT id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them -- and not by user_owner_b either, which is what makes batch 140's refusal a claim about the table rather than about a tenant boundary. It is a DENIED DELETE carrying an error_code and a change_before_ref, so it satisfies the other side of every cross-field CHECK that audit_log_a1 satisfies one side of: CTR-AUD-001 allOf[0] (a delete names what it deleted) and allOf[1] (a non-succeeded outcome carries an error).

security_event_a1.role: the security event of workspace_a, SECURITY-4. It carries NO ACTOR -- §9.1's own example of this family is a "replay anomaly", which is a pattern rather than somebody's act -- so it is the row that exercises app.security_events' both-or-neither actor constraint in the absent direction. It is the row `service-sees-zero-security-events` is about, which is the case the CI negative control for that table rests on.

security_event_b1.role: the security event of workspace_b, with an IDENTIFIED ACTOR, so the both-or-neither constraint is satisfied in both directions by real rows rather than only permitted by a CHECK. It is the far side of a boundary that refuses both sides identically: §8.4 marks "Security event details" `P` for the owner and RFC-2026-012 classifies the family server-only, so neither owner reaches their own.

knowledge_b1_business.role: BUSINESS-LEVEL knowledge under business_b1, on the far side of the tenant boundary. §8.6 case 5 and §12.6/1: every A-side identity attacks it while holding its EXACT id, and user_owner_b reads it, so the negative is not satisfied by an empty table. Its kind is `voice`.

notification_editor_a.role: An inbox row in workspace_a addressed to user_editor_a. THIS IS THE SYMBOL THAT PROVES THE USER HALF OF batch 051's two-term policy, and no earlier fixture row could carry it: every tenant table before app.notifications is scoped by workspace alone, so no case in this suite could distinguish two ACTIVE MEMBERS OF ONE WORKSPACE by row. user_owner_a holds this id exactly, is an active owner of the workspace it belongs to, and cannot read it -- which is what fails if `user_id = (select auth.uid())` is ever dropped from the predicate while `app.is_active_member(workspace_id)` remains. Its delivery_state is `failed` with a `transient` failure_class, so the fixture exercises CTR-NTF-001 allOf[2] in the branch that requires a class.

notification_owner_a.role: An inbox row in workspace_a addressed to user_owner_a: the POSITIVE this batch's negatives are measured against. Without a case that reads something, every refusal beside it is satisfied by an empty table. Its delivery_state is `delivered` with no failure_class, which is CTR-NTF-001 allOf[3] -- the rule independent testing of that contract added after finding `state: delivered` with `failure_class: permanent` accepted -- and it carries a null read_at so the `mark read` case has an unread row to change.

notification_owner_b.role: An inbox row in workspace_b addressed to user_owner_b: the far side of the tenant boundary. §12.6/1 and §8.6/5 -- every A-side identity attacks it while holding its EXACT id, and user_owner_b reads it, so the negative is not satisfied by an empty table. Its delivery_state is `suppressed_duplicate`, the fourth of CTR-NTF-001's states and the one ID-005 requires be visible in a result ('a suppression that is invisible in the result cannot be audited'), so the fixture loads all four states across four rows rather than leaving two permitted by a CHECK and never satisfied. Its read_at is null, as every loaded notification's is: a `no-effect` witness asserts a VALUE, and null is the value a refused mark-read would have changed.

notification_suspended_a.role: An inbox row in workspace_a ADDRESSED TO user_suspended_a, and the symbol that proves the MEMBERSHIP half of batch 051's two-term policy. §12.6/5 requires a suspended member to see zero TENANT rows, and a notification is a tenant row -- unlike 010's user profile, which that batch's header explicitly places outside the sentence. Against a table with nothing addressed to the suspended member the assertion is satisfied by an empty result that means nothing; this row is what makes `suspended-a-sees-zero-notifications` fail if `app.is_active_member(workspace_id)` is ever dropped while the user term remains. Its delivery_state is `queued`.

outbox_event_a.role: The event_id of workspace A's outbox row, and the event workspace A's consumer ledger row records having consumed. Added by batch 050 because a consumer ledger's whole mechanism is that ONE ROW NAMES ANOTHER ROW'S IDENTITY: CTR-EVT-001 makes event_id the envelope's required identity, app.consumer_ledger is unique on (workspace_id, consumer, event_id), and a generated id would make that pair unreproducible. Its subject is business_a1, which is where an event about a Business records the Business -- this family carries no business_profile_id column.

outbox_event_b.role: The event_id of workspace B's outbox row, and the event workspace B's ledger row records. The two ledger rows name the SAME consumer in two workspaces, which is what makes workspace_id's place in the natural key legible as data rather than only as a constraint. Its subject is business_b1.

page_a1.role: page under business_a1, inside the editor scope

page_a1_archived.role: third page under business_a1, ARCHIVED, under a LIVE Business. Added by batch 040 because its knowledge INSERT policy carries §11.3's archive clause TWICE — once for the Business and once for the Page — and the Page half had no row to be about: business_a3_archived is archived at the Business level, so a refusal there proves nothing about the second clause. This row is the only place in the fixture where the two parents disagree, which is what makes `owner-a-cannot-create-a-knowledge-item-under-an-archived-page` a case about the Page and not about its Business.

page_a1_sibling.role: second page under business_a1, in the SAME Business as page_a1. Added by batch 021 as the row §8.6 case 4 is about: page_a2 is under a different Business, so a member refused it has been refused by BUSINESS scope and case 4 — which is about Page scope inside one Business — would be satisfied by case 3's control. It is a new Page rather than a reuse of page_a2 for the reason business_a3_archived is a new Business: one fixture row carrying two unrelated controls is how a case starts failing for the other one's reason.

page_a2.role: page under business_a2, deliberately outside the editor scope

page_b1.role: page under business_b1, on the far side of the tenant boundary

user_editor_a.role: editor scoped to business_a1 and page_a1

user_owner_b.role: active owner of workspace_b, the other tenant

user_page_editor_a.role: active editor of workspace_a scoped to ONE PAGE, page_a1. Added by batch 021 because §8.6 case 4 — 'Same Business + allowed Page A but row Page B → deny' — cannot be carried by any identity §12.6 names: user_editor_a and user_approver_a are both scoped at BUSINESS level, and a business scope admits every Page beneath it by §7's own definition. Case 4 needs a member whose scope is a single Page and a second Page under the SAME Business to be refused, which is page_a1_sibling.

workspace_a.role: tenant A — the workspace every A-side identity belongs to

workspace_b.role: tenant B — the workspace nothing on the A side may ever reach

meta_connection_a.role: the Meta connection workspace_a holds, and the parent of every other batch 110 row on the A side: the social account discovered under it, the credential reference in `private` that names it, and the webhook delivery that would resolve to it. It carries an `_a` suffix because a connection is a tenant-owned row (§4's ERD reads WORKSPACE ||--o{ META_CONNECTION), unlike the global catalog rows this file also holds. Every batch 110 case that addresses it is a refusal, and the assertion is never 'A cannot reach B's row': no client identity reaches app.meta_connections at all, because §8.3 grants a HEALTH PROJECTION rather than the row and the read allowlist is empty. The one role holding a grant is app_worker, and what refuses it is row level security -- which is what the CI negative control for that table rests on.

meta_connection_b.role: the same row for workspace_b, and it is not decoration. A refusal that holds for one tenant because the other tenant has no row is a refusal about a missing fixture, so both sides carry a connection and a discovered social account, and the batch's substitute for a cross-tenant claim -- 'both owners are refused identically, at the same layer, with the same message' -- is about two real rows. It is also what makes app.social_accounts' workspace-scoped natural key legible as data: the SAME external account hash is loaded on both sides, and the unique constraint is over (workspace_id, external_account_hash), so neither insert can report that the other tenant already holds that account.

research_run_a1.role: the BUSINESS-LEVEL research run of business_a1: page_context_profile_id is NULL. It is the parent of the A-side source, snapshot, evidence and suggestion, and the row every positive in batch 070 addresses. It exercises the `then` branch of the run's restrictive narrowing -- app.member_scope_admits_business -- which user_editor_a (scoped business_a1) and user_page_editor_a (scoped page_a1, which 021 counts as covering its parent Business) both pass and user_owner_a passes by holding no scope row at all.

research_run_a1_page.role: the PAGE-LEVEL research run of business_a1, restricted to page_a1. It exercises the `else` branch of the same narrowing -- app.member_scope_admits_page -- and it is the positive half of §8.6 case 4: user_page_editor_a is scoped to page_a1 and must reach it. Without a row of this shape the Page branch of batch 070's case expression could be inverted without any case failing, which is the state 061's fixture note calls a branch no row exercises.

research_run_a1_sibling_page.role: the research run of business_a1 restricted to page_a1_sibling, and the negative half of §8.6 case 4. user_page_editor_a is scoped to page_a1, so a refusal here is refusal by PAGE scope inside a Business the member is otherwise admitted to -- which research_run_a2 cannot demonstrate, because a refusal there is refusal by BUSINESS scope and that is case 3. It is also the parent of research_source_a1_sibling_page, which is what carries the same claim one level down.

research_run_a2.role: the research run of business_a2, which is deliberately OUTSIDE user_editor_a's member scope. §8.6 case 3 -- 'same Workspace, allowed Business A, row Business B, deny' -- and the row that makes the Business branch of the narrowing a negative rather than a claim. user_owner_a holds no scope row and must still reach it, which is 021's reading of §7 and the control for the other half.

research_run_b1.role: the research run of business_b1 under workspace_b, held by its EXACT id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. §8.6 case 5, and the parent of the B-side source, evidence and suggestion so that each of those cross-tenant refusals is about a real row rather than about an empty table.

research_source_a1.role: the citation research_run_a1 made, and the parent of the A-side snapshot and evidence. It needs a symbol where a knowledge version and a member scope do not, and the rule is this catalog's own: a source has NO natural key. Batch 070 refuses to invent `unique (research_run_id, source_uri)`, because nothing says a run cites a URL once -- a run may reach the same page under two queries -- so a source is addressed by its id or by nothing.

research_source_a1_sibling_page.role: the citation research_run_a1_sibling_page made, and the row that carries batch 070's central claim about a CHILD: a source has no page column of its own, so its reach is its run's reach, resolved by a restrictive policy through app.research_runs. Without it, the whole child-narrowing design is asserted only for a business-level parent -- which is the branch that would still work if somebody replaced the exists() with app.member_scope_admits_business(workspace_id, business_profile_id).

research_source_b1.role: the citation research_run_b1 made. It exists so the cross-tenant refusals on app.research_sources, and the 'both owners are refused identically' substitute on app.research_snapshots, are about two real rows on two sides of the boundary rather than about one side and an absence. Its snapshot carries a DIFFERENT content hash from the A side's, so a capture is distinguishable from a copy of itself.

research_evidence_a1.role: the evidence item of research_source_a1, naming the A-side capture by its CONTENT HASH rather than by a foreign key -- which is §10's 'preserve permitted hash/citation metadata' expressed as a column. It needs a symbol because an evidence row has no natural key at all: nothing says a source supports one piece of evidence, and inventing a uniqueness so a case could address it without a constant would be a product decision written into a constraint. It is the row §8.6 case 9 is live on, because §5 names evidence the one immutable object of this family.

research_evidence_b1.role: the evidence item of research_source_b1, held by its exact id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. It carries a NULL snapshot_content_hash where the A side's carries a digest, so the nullable branch of research_evidence_snapshot_hash_is_a_digest is exercised by a real row and the two sides of the boundary are distinguishable rather than copies.

research_suggestion_a1.role: the suggestion research_run_a1 proposes, and the row §8.2's 'Suggestion save/dismiss/use' is asserted on from five identities: the owner and the editor may stamp a verb, the approver's P and the viewer's N may not, and the suspended member sees nothing. It is loaded with all three verb timestamps NULL, so every save/dismiss/use case writes a value the row did not already hold -- a case that set what was already there would pass against a database where the write did nothing (030's fixture rule).

research_suggestion_b1.role: the suggestion research_run_b1 proposes. It is loaded DISMISSED where the A side's is untouched, so the pair is two distinguishable rows and the cross-tenant write case -- workspace A's owner stamping `used_at` on workspace B's suggestion while holding its exact id -- is refused against a row whose research_suggestions_one_outcome constraint would ALSO have refused it. The case therefore names `saved_at`, which no constraint objects to, so the refusal it observes can only be the policy.

content_item_a1.role: the BUSINESS-LEVEL content item of business_a1: page_context_profile_id is NULL. It is the row every positive in batch 080 addresses, the parent of content_version_a1 and therefore, one level further down, of the A-side variant and quality review. It exercises the `then` branch of the item's restrictive narrowing -- app.member_scope_admits_business -- which user_editor_a (scoped business_a1) and user_page_editor_a (scoped page_a1, which 021 counts as covering its parent Business) both pass, and which user_owner_a passes by holding no scope row at all. It is loaded `draft`, because every case that moves a status is a REFUSAL and a row already in the state a case names would make that refusal indistinguishable from a write that did nothing.

content_item_a1_page.role: the PAGE-LEVEL content item of business_a1, restricted to page_a1. It exercises the `else` branch of the same narrowing -- app.member_scope_admits_page -- and it is the positive half of §8.6 case 4: user_page_editor_a is scoped to page_a1 and must reach it. Without a row of this shape the Page branch of batch 080's case expression could be inverted without any case failing, which is the state 061's fixture note calls a branch no row exercises.

content_item_a1_sibling_page.role: the content item of business_a1 restricted to page_a1_sibling, and the negative half of §8.6 case 4. user_page_editor_a is scoped to page_a1, so a refusal here is refusal by PAGE scope inside a Business the member is otherwise admitted to -- which content_item_a2 cannot demonstrate, because a refusal there is refusal by BUSINESS scope and that is case 3. It carries a version of its own, and that version is what makes the CHILD narrowing falsifiable: app.content_versions has no page column, so a version of this item is reachable only if its item is.

content_item_a2.role: the content item of business_a2, which is deliberately OUTSIDE user_editor_a's member scope. §8.6 case 3 -- 'same Workspace, allowed Business A, row Business B, deny' -- and the row that makes the Business branch of the narrowing a negative rather than a claim. user_owner_a holds no scope row and must still reach it, which is 021's reading of §7 and the control for the other half.

content_item_b1.role: the content item of business_b1 under workspace_b, held by its EXACT id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. §8.6 case 5, and the parent of content_version_b1 so that each cross-tenant refusal one level down is about a real row rather than about an empty table.

content_version_a1.role: version 1 of content_item_a1, and the one row in this family that gets a symbol DESPITE having a natural key. (workspace_id, business_profile_id, content_item_id, version_no) is unique, so a case could address it as 'version 1 of content_item_a1' exactly as batch 020's cases address a business version -- and the variant and the quality review hanging off it could not. Those two are addressed by their CONTENT VERSION ID, and a case that reached it through a join on app.content_versions would be asking two tables' policies one question and reporting the answer as though it were about one. So the version is named here, and the cost of the symbol is paid once instead of in every child's attribution.

content_version_b1.role: version 1 of content_item_b1, held by its exact id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. It is the parent of the B-side variant and quality review, so the cross-tenant refusals on those two tables are about real rows on both sides of the boundary rather than about one side and an absence. Its body differs from the A side's, so the two are distinguishable rows rather than copies.

quality_review_a1.role: the quality review of content_version_a1. It needs a symbol because a review has NO natural key: nothing in §4.6 says a version is reviewed once, a rule-set version may be re-run, and inventing a unique constraint so a case could address one without a symbol would be writing a product decision into a schema -- the rule this catalog has applied since batch 040's knowledge item. It is loaded `warn` with one finding carrying a rule_code and a message_th, so quality_reviews_findings_carry_code_and_message is a constraint a real row satisfies rather than one nothing exercises.

quality_review_b1.role: the quality review of content_version_b1, held by its exact id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. It is loaded `block` where the A side's is `warn`, so the pair is two distinguishable rows: a cross-tenant read that returned the wrong tenant's review would be visible as a different status rather than as an identical copy.

content_version_a1_sibling_page.role: version 1 of content_item_a1_sibling_page, and the second symbol in this family added for a row that already has a natural key. It exists so that the variant and the quality review hanging off it can be addressed by a CONSTANT rather than through a join, which is what makes the two-level chain -- variant through version through item -- falsifiable in the NEGATIVE direction. Without it, app.content_variants and app.quality_reviews would carry a positive for the chain and no case that fails when the chain is cut, which is the state 070's fixture note calls a branch no row exercises.

quality_review_a1_sibling_page.role: the quality review of content_version_a1_sibling_page, and the row `pinned-editor-a-cannot-see-the-quality-review-of-a-sibling-target-item` is about. user_page_editor_a is admitted to business_a1 and must still be refused the verdict on an item pinned to a sibling Page -- a refusal that has to resolve two tables up, through the version to the item, because a review carries neither a page column nor an item column of its own.

content_target_destination_a1.role: THE DESTINATION OF FOUR A-SIDE TARGETS, AND A UUID THAT NAMES NO ROW IN THIS REPOSITORY. app.content_targets.social_account_id carries NO foreign key: §6's registry gives "business-channel/social FK" to batch 111 and batch 081 is the placeholder contract that withholds it. app.social_accounts exists on disk in 110_meta_connector.sql and fixes no id -- 110's fixture addresses its rows by (workspace_id, external_account_hash) and lets `id` default -- so there is no social account uuid here to point at, and a subselect resolving one would make the missing key invisible by producing a target that looked correctly bound. Batch 080 met the same choice on generation_run_id and wrote NULL rather than a plausible uuid; social_account_id is NOT NULL, so the equivalent is a symbol that resolves to nothing. WHEN BATCH 111 ADDS THE KEY THIS SYMBOL MUST BE REPOINTED AT A SOCIAL ACCOUNT THAT EXISTS AND THE FIXTURE WILL STOP LOADING UNTIL IT IS -- which is the intended failure, because a fixture that kept loading through the addition of a foreign key is one whose rows never depended on it.

content_target_destination_a2.role: A SECOND DESTINATION UNDER THE SAME ITEM, and the only fixture row in batch 081 that is about this table rather than about its parent's scope. §4.6's rule is "unique active target \u0e15\u0e48\u0e2d content item/social account" -- a PAIR -- and a fixture with one target per item would load identically against an index keyed on the item alone, so this row is what makes that substitution fail to load. It is also the UNPINNED target, which is what gives content_targets_variant_scope_fk's MATCH SIMPLE skip and the nullable pin a row rather than a comment. It names no social account for the reason content_target_destination_a1 does not, and carries the same repointing debt to batch 111.

content_target_destination_b1.role: the destination of workspace_b's target, held by its exact id by every A-side identity and reached by none of them. It is DISTINCT from content_target_destination_a1 on purpose: nothing in this schema would refuse two tenants naming one social account -- the column is resolved against nothing at all -- so a fixture that pointed both sides at one destination would be modelling that gap as though it were a design rather than recording it in the work package's open blockers, which is where it is. Carries the same repointing debt to batch 111 as the two above.

_why_a_knowledge_item_needs_a_symbol_whe: Batch 040 adds FIVE symbols and no earlier batch added more than four, which is worth explaining rather than leaving as a number. A version row is addressed by its parent and its ordinal, a member scope by its member and its target, an industry assignment by the Business it belongs to -- every one of those is a natural key some document fixes. A KNOWLEDGE ITEM HAS NONE. Nothing in §4, §5 or §8 says a Business holds one voice profile, and inventing a `unique (business_profile_id, kind)` so that the fixture could address a row without a symbol would be encoding a product decision into a constraint in order to save five constants. So the items are named here and their versions are not: app.knowledge_item_versions makes (knowledge_item_id, version_number) unique, and every case that addresses a version addresses it through an item id this file fixes.
_no_symbol_for_a_member_scope_row: Batch 021 creates app.workspace_member_scopes and adds NO symbol for a row in it, for the same reason batch 020 added none for a version row. A member scope is identified by the member it belongs to and the target it names — (workspace_id, user_id, scope_type, business_profile_id, page_context_profile_id) is unique in 021_member_scope.sql — and every id in that tuple is already fixed here, so a case addresses an existing scope row exactly without a sixth constant to keep in step with the fixture. The two symbols batch 021 DID add are a member and a Page, because §8.6 case 4 needs a member scoped to one Page and a second Page under the same Business, and §12.6's list contains neither.
_no_symbol_for_a_version_row: Batch 020 creates two immutable version tables and adds NO symbol for their rows, which is a deliberate narrowing of the draft this batch grew from. A version is identified by its parent and its ordinal — (business_profile_id, version_number) and (page_context_profile_id, version_number) are unique constraints in 020_business.sql — so the immutability and cross-tenant cases address an EXISTING version row exactly, through ids this catalog already fixes, and the fixture inserts those rows with the id column defaulting to gen_random_uuid(). Nothing is weakened: §12.6's control is that tenant A holds tenant B's real id and still cannot reach the row, and business_b1's id is fixed here. Six more derived uuids would have been six more constants to keep in step with a fixture, bought with no assertion the natural key does not already make.
_no_symbol_for_an_industry_assignment: Batch 030 creates app.industry_assignments and adds NO symbol for a row in it, for the same reason batch 020 added none for a version row and batch 021 none for a member scope. §4's ERD makes the assignment zero-or-one per Business and 030_industry.sql makes (workspace_id, business_profile_id) unique, so a Business names at most one assignment and every case addresses it through ids this catalog already fixes. What batch 030 DID add is one Business and three global rows: the Business because the permitted INSERT needs a live target with no assignment, and the global rows because a catalog no case can address is a catalog no case can be about.
_no_symbol_for_a_billing_subscription_or: Batch 130 creates app.billing_subscriptions and app.plan_entitlements and adds NO symbol for a row in either, for the same reason batch 020 added none for a version row, 021 none for a member scope and 030 none for an industry assignment. A subscription is addressed by the workspace it belongs to -- 130_billing.sql makes (workspace_id) unique among the states that are not `canceled`, which is §1's "one billable subscription per workspace" -- and an entitlement by the published revision and the feature key, which (billing_plan_version_id, feature_key) makes unique. Every id in both tuples is already fixed here, so a case addresses an existing row exactly without another constant to keep in step with a fixture. What batch 130 DID add is two GLOBAL rows, because a catalog no case can address is a catalog no case can be about -- and because the two subscriptions naming the SAME plan revision id, one per tenant, is the only way this suite can assert that the catalog is global when no identity may read it.
_no_symbol_for_a_notification_preference: Batch 051 creates three tables and adds symbols for rows in ONE of them. A notification needs a symbol for the reason a knowledge item and an audit record do: it has no natural key a document fixes, and inventing a unique constraint so a case could address one without a symbol would be writing a product decision into a schema. A NOTIFICATION PREFERENCE has one -- (workspace_id, user_id, channel) is 051's composite primary key, and CTR-NTF-001 fixes the three channels -- so every id in that tuple is already here and a case addresses an existing row exactly. A PUSH SUBSCRIPTION REFERENCE needs none for a different and sharper reason: NO IDENTITY IN THIS SCHEMA MAY READ IT. Every case against private.push_subscription_references is refused at name resolution on the SCHEMA, identically, for every identity including the service, so a case never addresses a row by id at all; the fixture loads one row so those negatives are not satisfied by an empty table, and it is addressed by its credential_reference, which is unique. Batch 060 declined a symbol for private.ai_credential_references on exactly this ground and this is that decision unchanged, one secret table later.
_no_symbol_for_a_research_snapshot: Batch 070 creates five tables and adds symbols for rows in FOUR of them. A run, a source, an evidence item and a suggestion have no natural key any document fixes, and 070 refuses to invent one for each (nothing says a run cites a URL once, or that a source supports one piece of evidence), so each is addressed by an id fixed here. A RESEARCH SNAPSHOT HAS A NATURAL KEY AND GETS NO SYMBOL: 070_research.sql makes (workspace_id, research_source_id, content_hash) unique, because that triple is also what app.research_evidence.snapshot_content_hash has to name single-valued once §10's purge has removed the locator. So a case addresses a snapshot as `where research_source_id = $1 and content_hash = sha256(convert_to($2, 'utf8'))`, exactly as batch 010's cases address an invitation by its token digest, and the fixture composes the same digest from the same string. That is worth more than a symbol here rather than less: it is a demonstration that the hash IS an address, which is the whole reason §10 says to preserve it. The synthetic string it digests is this repository's own and is not captured material -- §9.2's prohibition on a full research snapshot names `fixture` in its own list of surfaces, so a fixture that carried a real page would violate the rule the table exists to hold.
_no_symbol_for_a_content_idea_a_variant_: Batch 080 creates five tables and adds symbols for rows in three of them, which is this catalog's own rule applied rather than a count anybody chose. A CONTENT IDEA is addressed by (workspace_id, client_request_id): §4.6 asks for "unique idempotency \u0e15\u0e48\u0e2d workspace" and 080_content.sql makes that a partial unique index, so the idea is named by the request that created it exactly as batch 050's job is named by its dedupe key. A CONTENT VARIANT is addressed by (content_version_id, platform): §4.6 asks for a "unique logical variant key" and the constraint spans the version, the platform and the variant type -- declared NULLS NOT DISTINCT, so the fixture's untyped variant is a single row that pair names. AND MOST CONTENT VERSIONS ARE ADDRESSED BY (content_item_id, version_no), which is unique, which is why the two that DO carry a symbol carry it for a reason that is not about addressing themselves: the variant and the quality review are addressed THROUGH a version id, and a case that resolved that id by joining app.content_versions would put two tables' policies behind one result. Batch 020 established that a version needs no symbol; batch 080 agrees with it and pays two constants where a child would otherwise borrow its parent's policy.
_no_symbol_for_a_content_target_and_thre: Batch 081 creates ONE table, adds NO symbol for a row in it, and adds three for a column of that row -- which is the first time this catalog has done that and is worth the sentence. A CONTENT TARGET HAS A NATURAL KEY: 081_content_targets.sql makes (content_item_id, social_account_id) unique among rows whose deleted_at is null, which is §4.6's "unique active target", so every case addresses a target as `where content_item_id = $1 and social_account_id = $2` out of ids fixed here -- the rule batch 020 set for a version row and 030, 051, 070 and 080 each applied in turn. THE DESTINATIONS ARE THE OPPOSITE CASE. social_account_id carries no foreign key, by §6's registry, which gives that key to batch 111; app.social_accounts fixes no id of its own; so the value is a bare uuid that a fixture writes and a case must hold, resolved against nothing, addressable through no other table's natural key. That is precisely the constant this catalog exists to fix, and fixing it is also what makes the missing key VISIBLE: three ids that name nothing are a reader's first evidence that nothing checks a destination. Batch 111 must repoint all three, and the fixture will refuse to load until it does.
